verdict: Lusha is a strong B2B contact-data and enrichment layer with Engage sequences and CRM sync — not a pipeline CRM. Score it as sales intelligence plugged into your CRM of record. This review is based on first-party Lusha documentation — not hands-on product testing. Public dollar pricing was not verified from lusha.com/pricing during research.
strengths: Verified contact/company data plus enrichment workflows
Browser extension prospecting on LinkedIn/Sales Navigator
Engage email sequences with AI writing assistance
Native CRM connectors (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Bullhorn)
Signals and AI recommendations for prioritization
weaknesses: Not a deal-pipeline CRM — weak on CRM methodology pipeline criteria
Credit consumption (especially phones) can surprise high-volume teams
Public list prices not verified in this research pass (Cloudflare)
Reporting is usage/ops oriented rather than sales forecasting
bestFor: SDR/BDR teams needing verified emails/dials and enrichment
RevOps cleaning CRM records and automating enrichment
notIdealFor: Buyers seeking an all-in-one pipeline CRM
Teams that need transparent verified public price cards before shortlisting
Orgs wanting dialer-first telephony CRM suites
tradeoffs: Data accuracy/enrichment depth vs CRM pipeline completeness
Credit flexibility vs unpredictable consumption at phone-heavy volume
Engage convenience vs dedicated sales-engagement platforms
recommendation: Choose Lusha when contact data quality and CRM enrichment are the buying criteria, and keep Pipedrive/HubSpot/Salesforce as the system of record. Confirm current Starter–Scale credit bundles on Lusha’s pricing page before purchase.
editorialNotes: Approved from Lusha first-party docs. handsOnTesting=false. Pricing amounts omitted (contactSales) because lusha.com/pricing was not successfully retrieved.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Workspace, Chrome/Edge extension, and Engage are documented as accessible prospecting surfaces; learning curve centers on credits/filters rather than CRM admin.
Lusha is sales intelligence/enrichment, not a visual deal pipeline CRM. Pipeline remains in the buyer’s CRM of record.
Engage sequences, connectors/API automation, and signal-triggered workflows are documented; depth depends on plan and CRM wiring.
Engage supports Gmail/Outlook sequences with AI writing help; not a full marketing ESP.
Analytics/usage dashboards and credit reporting are documented; classic CRM forecast reporting is not the product focus.
Filters, ICP/target profiles, workspace tables, and CRM field mapping provide moderate fit customization.
Native Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Bullhorn plus Zapier/Clay-style connectors and API.
Credit allocation, roles, and enrichment hygiene need ongoing ops attention, but lighter than enterprise CRM suites.
Scale plan, API, and bulk enrichment support growth; credit economics become the practical ceiling.
Public list prices not verified (Cloudflare); credit consumption risk versus RocketReach’s transparent ladder.

overallScoreRationale: Equal-weight CRM methodology average. Integrations and prospecting UX lift the score; pipeline-management and unverified paid pricing keep it mid-band. Not a hands-on lab score.
